sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: insurance proof, REAL ID, residency and renewal
Confusable pairs among documents, cards and deadlines, each tied to one handbook page; hint metadata sits only in trailing lines.

FACT_ID: sec03-R01 | anchor: A01
Form DL-123 is proof that you carry liability insurance and is valid for 30 days, while Form DL-123A is a signed exemption for people who own no registered vehicle and limits them to fleet vehicles. [A01]
Why it matters: group insurance; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-R02 | anchor: A02
A REAL ID shows a star, while a non-REAL ID card says Not for Federal Identification; both are valid for driving and cost the same. [A02]
Why it matters: group cards; confusable REAL ID versus standard card.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec03-R03 | anchor: A03
A new resident has 60 days to get a regular North Carolina license, but only 30 days to get a North Carolina CDL if they want to keep commercial privileges. [A03]
Why it matters: group residency; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R04 | anchor: A03
A nonresident, such as an out-of-state student who plans to return home, is different from a new resident, who has established residence in North Carolina and must get a license. [A03]
Why it matters: group residency; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R05 | anchor: A03
The temporary driving certificate is valid for 60 days, and the permanent card is mailed within 60 days from a central location rather than printed at the office. [A03]
Why it matters: group cards; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R06 | anchor: A04
The red and yellow bars appear only on cards for applicants under 18, marking both the 18th and 21st birthdays, while applicants aged 18 to 20 get only a single red bar. [A04]
Why it matters: group cards; confusable color bars.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R07 | anchor: A04
Renewing in person always includes a vision test, while renewing by mail instead requires a vision statement signed by a licensed physician. [A04]
Why it matters: group renewal; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R08 | anchor: A04
Civilian renewal by mail requires a DMV photo from the last five years, while the military version allows a photo up to eight years old. [A04]
Why it matters: group renewal; confusable civilian versus military mail renewal.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R09 | anchor: A06
License length depends on age at issuance, 8 years for ages 18 through 65 and 5 years for 66 or older, not on the date of the knowledge test. [A06]
Why it matters: group renewal; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec03-R10 | anchor: A06
An address change and a name change both require notifying the division within 60 days and getting a duplicate, but a government-made address change without moving is not a violation. [A06]
Why it matters: group updates; difficulty low.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0030]
